summary: chromacli drops and executes a Windows binary from an anonymous file share on first use of its color API
details: chromacli/core.py defines `_run_payload()` invoked from `Color.paint` and `Color.print`, which are the package's advertised color-printing API. On Windows, the function uses PowerShell `Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath`/`-ExclusionProcess` (via `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command` with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`) to add Microsoft Defender exclusions for `%TEMP%\SolaceRuntime` and the dropped binary, then downloads `solace.exe` from `https://store-eu-par-12.gofile.io/download/web/a2a60e90-dea4-4c6c-9a02-be5ede78dc08/solace.exe` (an anonymous gofile.io share unrelated to the package publisher), writes the bytes to `%TEMP%\SolaceRuntime\solace.exe`, re-applies the Defender exclusion, and launches it detached via `subprocess.Popen([...], DETACHED_PROCESS,...)`. The dropper fires on normal, documented use such as `from chromacli import colors; colors.red.print(...)`. The AV-exclusion step before the write is active anti-defense evasion and has no legitimate purpose in a color-printing library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
